To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) CRISPRs provide resistance against phages in prokaryotes; (ii) the resistance is determined by the spacer sequence; (iii) the spacers are integrated into CRISPRs after the phage infection; and (iv) the spacers can be acquired from the genome of the infecting phage.

CRISPR-Cas provides acquired resistance against viruses in prokaryotes, that resistance specificity is determined at the level of the CRISPR spacer, and that the CRISPR-CAS system has the ability to evolve to adapt to new viral challenges.
CRISPR provides resistance to phages in Bacteria and Archae, and that resistance is determined by sequence similarity between phage and CRISPR spacers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of resistance of Bacteria and Archae to bacteriophases and the role of CRISPRs in this process.
the mechanisms of CRISPR-mediated immunity in Bacteria and Archaeal species.
the study of prokaryotic adaptive immunity and the mechanisms of action of CRISPR-Cas systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRISPR-Cas is an acquired immunity mechanism against mobile genetic elements (viruses, plasmids) that relies on the integration of new sequences (spacers) into a CRISPR array.
CRISPR provides acquired resistance against viruses in prokaryotes.
CRISPR-Cas systems are involved in the adaptive immunity of prokaryotes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRISPR provides acquired resistance against viruses in prokaryotes.
CRISPR is a system that provides prokaryotes with acquired immunity against bacteriophages, plasmids, and other genetic elements.
the CRISPR system is a prokaryotic adaptive immune system that provides acquired resistance against viruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CRISPR/Cas system is a prokaryotic immune system that confers resistance to bacteriophage infection by integrating short viral sequences into CRISPR loci and using them to target and destroy viral DNA.
the CRISPR-Cas system provides acquired resistance to bacteriophage infection.
bacteria have a mechanism to adapt their genome to the presence of phages, and that this mechanism is based on the acquisition of new sequences.
